what_its_for: Lasmiditan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It helps relieve the pain and other symptoms of a migraine attack, such as nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound. It is NOT used to prevent migraines from happening — only to treat them once they start.
how_to_take: Take lasmiditan by mouth as a tablet. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Take it as soon as your migraine headache starts for the best results. You may take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first dose if your headache comes back or does not fully go away, but do not take more than 2 doses in any 24-hour period. IMPORTANT: Do NOT drive a car or operate heavy machinery for at least 8 hours after taking this medicine, even if you feel fine. This drug can seriously affect your ability to drive safely.
dosing: The usual dose is 50 mg, 100 mg, or 200 mg taken as a single tablet when a migraine starts. Your doctor will decide which dose is right for you. Do not take more than 200 mg in one dose and no more than 2 doses within 24 hours.
missed_dose: Lasmiditan is taken only when you have a migraine — it is not a daily medication. There is no regular dosing schedule, so a 'missed dose' does not apply in the usual sense. Simply take it when your next migraine begins, following the instructions your doctor gave you.
storage: Store lasmiditan at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep the tablets in their original container. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT drive, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires full alertness for at least 8 hours after taking lasmiditan — even if you feel okay. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid taking other medicines that cause sleepiness, such as sleep aids, anti-anxiety drugs, or certain pain medicines, without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor about ALL medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, as lasmiditan can interact with many other medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; shortness of breath; fast or irregular heartbeat; severe dizziness or fainting; unusual weakness or numbness; severe drowsiness; serotonin syndrome symptoms such as agitation, hallucinations, rapid heart rate, high fever, muscle stiffness or twitching, or loss of coordination. Also call your doctor if your migraines are not improving, if you are using this medicine more than 10 days per month (which can make headaches worse), or if you have any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Lasmiditan usually starts to work within 1 to 2 hours after taking it. Many people notice their migraine pain getting better within 2 hours. Results may vary from person to person. If your headache is not improving after the first dose, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours later, but contact your doctor if the medicine does not seem to be working for you.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older): Use with caution, as dizziness and falls may be a greater risk. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety during pregnancy is not fully known. Breastfeeding: It is not known if lasmiditan passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding while using this medicine. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Children: Lasmiditan is approved only for adults and should not be used in patients under 18 years of age.
